claim: The bonds carry a covenant requiring the Authority to set rates so it holds at least 1.25 times its annual debt service.
note: A margin requirement rather than a payment requirement.

claim: The Official Statement prints a single coverage ratio, and every forecast year clears 1.25.
note: 1.60, 1.37, 1.36, 1.37, 1.43, 1.44. Reproduces from the table's own rows.

claim: Footnote 1 on that table reads: Includes Other Pledged Revenues.
note: Read on the page in both pdftotext extraction modes. This is what makes the separation arithmetic rather than inference.

claim: On the revenue actually pledged, five of the six forecast years fall below 1.25.
note: 1.35, 1.12, 1.13, 1.12, 1.18, 1.19. The document prints only the combined figure; the separation is ours and is labelled as ours wherever it appears.

claim: In 2026 and 2028 the airport's own operations do not cover its debt service at all.
note: $83.0m against $84.7m in 2026, $90.2m against $90.8m in 2028. Net Revenues less the Exhibit E designations.

claim: The Coverage Account is topped up monthly at the Authority's own discretion and capped at 25 percent of that year's debt service.
note: Ninth in the flow of funds. Nothing obliges the Authority to make the deposit.

claim: The forecast assumes the Coverage Account at exactly its contractual ceiling in five of six years.
note: 25.00 percent of aggregate annual debt service in every year except 2027, which is 23.23 percent.

claim: From 2025 the entire designated line is slot-machine tax revenue. Gas royalty is designated at zero in every year from 2020 through 2030.
note: Exhibit E itemises the line by component. What was designated 2020 through 2023 was federal pandemic relief; nothing at all was designated in 2024.

claim: The airlines committed that money for 2026 through 2028. The forecast carries the same figure into 2029 and 2030.
note: The Airline Operating Agreements expire Dec. 31, 2028. The bonds run to 2056.

claim: No debt service entered the airline rate base in 2021, 2022, 2023 or 2024.
note: Table IV. The row reads zero in all four years.

claim: Interest on the 2021 bonds was capitalized through Feb. 1, 2025 and on the 2023 bonds through April 1, 2025.
note: This is why the rate base carried no terminal debt for four years.

claim: The audited charge per boarded passenger fell to $7.34 in 2024, the lowest in the ten-year audited series.
note: Reproduces as $36,444,805 of rate base costs over 4,964,361 enplanements.

claim: The Authority's consultant forecasts the charge rising every year, from $15.71 in 2025 to $20.53 in 2030.
note: Reproduces as airline payments over enplanements in all six years.

claim: Four different measures are published under the name cost per enplaned passenger.
note: For 2024 the audited report gives $7.34 where the bond statement gives $11.56. No figure on this site is subtracted from a figure on another basis.

claim: The 2021 statement forecast four years under two recovery cases. Two of four fall below 1.25 in the base case and four of four in the slow case.
note: Stated by case. The two cases are not added together, which would count the same calendar years twice.

claim: The Authority told the Post-Gazette $17.64 for 2026 after filing $19.13 with investors in April 2025.
note: A budget adopted later can legitimately differ from a forecast made earlier. The higher figure went to the lenders. This is a question for the Authority, not a finding.

claim: Passengers arrived on forecast. The 2024 actual of 4,964,361 beat the 2021 base case of 4,924,000.
note: The cost forecast is the one that missed, not the passenger forecast.

claim: Whether a rising airline charge reaches a passenger as fare or as reduced service is disputed and is not settled here.
note: Five claims and five studies are adjudicated in the reporting. No study in the record tests Pittsburgh.

claim: The board approved the terminal at $1.1 billion in September 2017. It opened eight years and two months later.
note: Media is graded C in this reporting: a source of dates and statements, never of a figure computed with.

claim: Federal rules require an alternatives analysis for a master plan. The Authority has never published the one behind this decision.
note: Sections 901 through 907. What renovating the existing terminal would have cost has never been published.

claim: A rating agency reads the same discretionary money as a credit strength.
note: The availability of unique non-aviation revenue sources which can be applied on a discretionary basis.
